# Prerequisites {#sec-prerequisites}

## Installing Julia {#sec-installing}

Use **`juliaup`**, the official version manager. Do not install Julia through a system
package manager (`apt`, `brew`), which tends to ship outdated versions.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## macOS and Linux

```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.julialang.org | sh
```

## Windows

```powershell
winget install julia -s msstore
```
:::

Afterwards, `juliaup update` upgrades and `juliaup status` lists installed versions.

## Project environments {#sec-environments}

This is the most important concept in the chapter, and the one that differs most from
common practice in R.

In R, `install.packages()` installs into a global library shared by all your projects.
In Julia, each project has its own environment, described by two files:

- **`Project.toml`** — the direct dependencies you declared.
- **`Manifest.toml`** — the full resolved dependency tree, with exact versions of
  everything.

Together they make an analysis reproducible by construction: anyone who clones your
repository and runs `Pkg.instantiate()` gets exactly your versions.

::: {.r-equivalent}
**In R**

`Project.toml` + `Manifest.toml` play the role of `renv.lock`, but they are part of the
language rather than an add-on package. Activating an environment is the default
operation, not the exception.
:::

```{julia}
#| label: env-status
using Pkg
Pkg.status()
```

## This book's environment {#sec-book-environment}

```{julia}
#| label: versioninfo
versioninfo()
```

To reproduce the book:

```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd EcologicalAnalysesInJulia
julia --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()'
```

## Editor {#sec-editor}

**VS Code** with the official language extension is the standard recommendation: it
offers an integrated REPL, variable inspector, debugger and line-by-line evaluation
(`Shift+Enter`) — the functional equivalent of RStudio.

Alternatives: **Pluto.jl** (reactive notebooks, excellent for teaching) and any editor
with LSP support through `LanguageServer.jl`.

## Quarto {#sec-quarto}

This book is written in [Quarto](https://quarto.org), the direct successor to
`bookdown`. Since version 1.5, Quarto executes Julia blocks natively, without going
through Jupyter.

````markdown
```{{julia}}
#| label: example
1 + 1
```
````
